AI Capability Evolution Simulator. Models alternative AI architectures, training methods, tool systems, and safety controls before costly deployment.

This database covers the technology as item 211 entry 39 of Manon's "100 Ultra-Advanced Future Technologies" catalog, section "Intelligence Beyond Today's AI". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: theoretically plausible. Scaling laws predict capabilities from compute; simulating full architecture evolution is unvalidated.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: AI Capability Evolution Simulator - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: Models alternative AI architectures, training methods, tool systems, and safety controls before costly deployment.
body:
Known science foundations of AI Capability Evolution Simulator.

Neural scaling laws (Kaplan et al., 2020; Hoffmann/Chinchilla, 2022) predict loss from compute and data. Compute-forecasting models project training costs. AI safety researchers model takeoff scenarios. But simulating which architectures and training methods win — before training them — remains speculative modeling, not validated science.

Key quantity check (Largest training runs in FLOP / simulator prediction error in percent): computed ratio 5e+24 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.5. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: AI Capability Evolution Simulator - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Models alternative AI architectures, training methods, tool systems, and safety controls before costly deployment.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on AI Capability Evolution Simulator.

Scaling laws describe loss, not capabilities or safety. Architecture space is vast and poorly parameterized. Simulations risk false confidence in deployment decisions.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 25 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is frontier training compute vs architectures compared at 25 orders of magnitude (frontier training compute larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

Unresolved problems for AI Capability Evolution Simulator, in priority order (research burden index 30, 3 blocking):

Validating architecture predictions (severity 3/3, tractability 1/3, BLOCKING; priority 12).

From loss curves to capabilities (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

Modeling safety controls faithfully (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.
